html:
Miwkoʔ Waaliʔ means "Miwok land". On this map it marks the lower Mokelumne and Cosumnes rivers, at the eastern edge of the Sacramento and San Joaquin delta in central California. This was the country of the Plains Miwok, part of the larger Miwok family of peoples.

They lived in villages on river banks, gathered acorns and seeds, fished for salmon and hunted waterfowl in the marshes. Their neighbours were the Nisenan to the north and the Yokuts to the south.

In the early 1800s Spanish missions in the Bay Area drew in many Plains Miwok. Malaria in 1833 and the Gold Rush after 1848 then killed most of those who remained.
